newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta coffee ends flat.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta coffee ends flat.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were little moved in the afternoon and prices ended Friday almost unchanged.
Traders said activity was restricted by lack of fresh fundamental news and the Independence Day holiday in New York.
Traders said just 400 lots changed hands in the afternoon, bringing the day's tally to 2,018 lots.
"People were just jobbing around their positions," said one. Trading will stay subdued until New York reopens on Monday afternoon.
September, the London benchmark, drifted within a $15 band to finish the day unchanged at $1,795 a tonne. Other traded months flat to $5 lower.
On the charts, the London contract could attempt to push higher and break out of a tightening range but may not have enough upside momentum to sustain the move.

"The range is tightening...but on a tightening like this you normally have quite a good move at the end of it," said Susan Rigg at Chart Analysis. "I wouldn't be at all surprised if it didn't try to rally but I'm not sure it's going to get very far."

According to U.S. forecaster WSC, cold air building over Argentina on Friday was expected to pass off to the south of Brazil's coffee belt as the warm, high pressure dominating the area continued its hold over the region.
In other news, Kenya has suspended its weekly coffee auctions for the next two weeks because of acute shortages.
Traders said unless Brazil weather offers some surprises, coffee could face a retracement on the back of bearish fundamental inputs.
Stocks of nearby green coffee in the hands of roasters and traders were building up in Europe and the United States as demand for finished products heads lower.

Coffee consumption normally drops during northern hemisphere summer. But demand is further hit by the increases in retail prices following the recent price rally. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
